core_obligations: Identify the new diagonal as a base change of the old.
Transfer flatness and unramifiedness through the definition.
difficulty_reason: For a cartesian square with X' = Y' x_Y X, the lemma proves (1) flatness of the diagonal X' -> X' x_{Y'} X' follows from flatness of X -> X x_Y X, and (2) base changes of weakly etale morphisms are weakly etale. The retained proof is written: the diagonal of X' over Y' is the base change of the diagonal of X over Y along the map Y' x_Y Y' -> Y x_Y Y' restricted to the fibre square (the author's one-line identification X' x_{Y'} X' = Y' x_{(Y x_Y Y)} (X x_Y X)), and flatness is preserved under base change (cited Morphisms lemma base-change-flat); part (2) adds the unramified half — also base-change stable — and reads off the definition. Retained author proof at lines 19012-19018.
